solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Modest nursing home's gleaming

indicators.note: a nurse holds a patient, so the first word here cradles the second within it

parts.note: a modest person is shy
in means at home

explanation.surface: A self-effacing care home has been polished till it shines.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gleaming has a bright polished surface, which is a close synonym.

clue.text: A few soon meet every so often

indicators.note: every so often means taking letters at regular intervals, here the first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: A handful of people will get together before long, now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Some, used of a number, means an unspecified small quantity, a handful.

clue.text: Famous writer, liberal one, featuring in glossy

parts.note: the crossword setter, the writer, refers to themself as I

indicators.note: featuring in means appearing within, so the letter for one goes inside the word for glossy

parts.note: lustrous means glossy
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A well-known author, one with liberal views, appears in a glossy magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Illustrious means celebrated and distinguished, a stronger synonym of well known.

clue.text: The erstwhile sultanate's palace attendant

parts.note: ye is an old spelling of the, as in Ye Olde Tea Shoppe
Oman is a sultanate in Arabia

explanation.surface: A servant at the royal palace of a former sultanate.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yeoman Warder or Yeoman of the Guard serves the British monarch at royal residences.

clue.text: One informs youth about new area for stock

parts.note: a grass is slang for an informer

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the youth's word goes round the letter for new

parts.note: a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: An informer tells a young man about a fresh place to keep cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: GRASS is British slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Grazing land is where livestock, the farmer's stock, are kept and fed.

clue.text: Troops armed us on manoeuvres in borders of Gabon

indicators.note: in means the jumbled letters sit within the outer letters of the country
borders of means the outside letters of the word Gabon
troops on manoeuvres move about, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Soldiers have armed us during an exercise on Gabon's frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on manoeuvres' rearranges ARMED US into UARDSME, which goes 'in' G and N, the 'borders of' Gabon.
explanation.definitionFit: Guardsmen are soldiers of a guards regiment, so collectively they are troops.

clue.text: Involved in hearing, woman's beginning to finish

indicators.note: the opening letter of the woman's name is taken from the start and sent to the end

parts.note: Laura is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman at a court hearing is there from start to end.
explanation.definitionFit: Aural describes anything to do with the ear and the sense of hearing.

clue.text: Wastepipe controlling a river's main force?

indicators.note: something controlling another holds it in its grip, so the pipe's word surrounds the rest

parts.note: a sewer is a waste pipe
the Po is a river in Italy

explanation.surface: A drainage pipe regulates a river's main flow.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is the sea, so a main force is naval strength; the '?' flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea power is a nation's naval strength, its military force on the open ocean.

clue.text: Ringmaster at heart of 10

indicators.note: at heart of keeps only the central letters of the other entry's answer, stripping two from each end

parts.note: 10 is the across answer at 10, REALITY

explanation.surface: A circus ringmaster stands at the centre of the action.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring is a boxing ring: Muhammad Ali was its master.
explanation.definitionFit: Muhammad Ali, the great boxer, was master of the boxing ring.

clue.text: Train ready-made radical fantasist

indicators.note: to train something is to shape it into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for radical

explanation.surface: A trainee extremist takes on views off the peg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a verb or a railway carriage, but it signals the anagram of READY-MADE; 'radical' is not a second anagram signal but supplies R.
explanation.definitionFit: A daydreamer drifts into fanciful imaginings, as a fantasist does.

clue.text: State initially manages antiquated cells

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word manages

parts.note: antiquated means old
ova are egg cells

explanation.surface: A country is said to start out running prisons that are out of date.
explanation.definitionFit: Moldova is an independent European country, a sovereign state between Romania and Ukraine.

clue.text: The truth about post- revolution Italy

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: Italy after a revolution has its letters overturned and rearranged

explanation.surface: A political claim about how things really stand in Italy after an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Reality is what actually is, the facts of the matter, so it equals the truth.

clue.text: Study Dutch welfare worker hiring German gossip

parts.note: to scan is to study closely

indicators.note: an employer hiring someone takes them in, so the worker's word takes in the letter for German

parts.note: an almoner was a hospital social worker

explanation.surface: A report on a Dutch social worker taking on a German member of staff.
explanation.walkthrough: An ALMONER was the old British name for a hospital social worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandalmonger spreads scurrilous tales about others, so is a gossip in the personal sense.

clue.text: Tree student has info on each branch first

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the following pieces come along in sequence after the info word

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
a log is a cut length of a tree branch
1st, read as IST, is the abbreviation for first

explanation.surface: A pupil of trees gathers data on every bough before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tree' is a family tree, not a plant; 'first' is written 1ST with the 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A genealogist traces family histories, so studies the family tree of ancestors.

clue.text: Gorging on these, front of tummy drops into trousers?

definitions.text: Gorging on these, front of tummy drops into trousers?

indicators.note: into means the shifted letters are put inside the word for trousers

parts.note: jeans are trousers

indicators.note: front of with drops says the opening letter of the tummy word falls down
drops sends that opening letter to the bottom, the end of the word

parts.note: belly is another word for tummy

explanation.surface: Eat too many sweets and your stomach spills over your waistband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front of ... drops' sends the tummy word's opening letter to its foot, and that result sits 'into' the trousers after their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Jelly beans are small sugary sweets that are easy to eat by the handful.

clue.text: Fawn found in English vineyard

parts.note: a cru is a French vineyard or its growth of wine

explanation.surface: A young deer turns up among the vines of an English wine estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is a pale greyish-yellow colour, much like fawn, the light brown shade.

clue.text: Factory girl I enlisted returns for long spells

parts.note: a mill is a factory

indicators.note: returns means the combined letters are read in the opposite direction
someone enlisted is taken into a group, so I goes inside the girl's name

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A mill girl's words: having joined up, she comes back for long periods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enlisted' puts I into the girl's name before 'returns' turns the whole group round, giving AINNE read backwards as ENNIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Millennia are periods of a thousand years each, very long spells of time.

clue.text: Latin American orator once hugs female, thus?

parts.note: US means American

indicators.note: something that hugs another wraps around it, so the orator's name encloses the letter for female

parts.note: Tully is the old English name for Cicero, the Roman orator

explanation.surface: A Latin American, a former speaker, embraces a woman in a certain way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thus' asks how the Latin American hugs her, so the surface itself supplies the definition, with the '?' marking it.
explanation.definitionFit: The hug described is full of desire, so 'thus' means with passionate longing.

clue.text: Damn slow learner holds individual up

indicators.note: holds means the learner's word keeps the other piece inside it

parts.note: a dunce is a slow learner

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: one means an individual

explanation.surface: A curse on the dim pupil who keeps a single classmate back.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses, giving ENO, and 'holds' places it after the learner's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To denounce is to condemn publicly, and to damn is to condemn.

clue.text: Left ducks nibbling primarily among nuts? They need tying up

parts.note: a duck is a nil score in cricket, the letter O, so two ducks are OO

indicators.note: among means set in the middle of the other letters, so the pick goes inside the word for nuts

parts.note: nuts are a kind of seed

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of the word nibbling

explanation.surface: The ducks that are left peck first at the nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is cricket's word for a score of nothing, hence O. The '?' marks the cryptic definition of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfinished details are tied up at the end of a story, like the loose strands of a rope.

clue.text: Manage food transportation cost

definitions.meaning: to ... is to get on or manage, as in how did you ...
the price of a ticket on a bus or train

explanation.definitionFit: The one word covers getting along, a menu's offerings, and the money paid for a journey.

clue.text: Bar student learned somehow to inspire affection

indicators.note: somehow means in some way or other, so the remaining letters are rearranged
bar means except or excluding, so a letter is removed

parts.note: L is a learner, the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A law student somehow learned how to win people over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' removes L from LEARNED to leave EARNED, whose letters the final indicator word shuffles. Bar also suggests a law student, a misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear is to make someone liked, to inspire their fondness.

clue.text: Graduates with very senior teacher ruin singer

parts.note: BAs are Bachelors of Arts, graduates
so means very
a prof is a professor
to undo someone is to ruin them

explanation.surface: Graduates and a very senior academic bring about someone's downfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A basso profondo is a singer with an extremely low bass voice.

clue.text: What scouts do in playground supported by this Parisian

indicators.note: in a down clue supported by means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a playground
ce is French for this

explanation.surface: Boy Scouts' antics in a playground, backed by a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: A recce, short for reconnaissance, is a scouting trip, so it is what scouts do.
explanation.definitionFit: Military scouts carry out reconnaissance, surveying ground ahead, which is a recce.

clue.text: Charge 50 envoys, barring every second

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for 50

indicators.note: barring every second letter leaves the first, third and fifth letters of envoys

explanation.surface: Charging fifty diplomats, but not every other one.
explanation.definitionFit: A levy is a tax or fee imposed, which is a charge.

clue.text: Is it put out in case awful rodent pokes its head in?

definitions.text: Is it put out in case awful rodent pokes its head in?

indicators.note: pokes in together say one piece is pushed into the middle of another
with pokes this says the rodent's initial is pushed inside the jumbled letters
awful suggests the two words are messed up and their letters rearranged
its head means the first letter of the word rodent

explanation.surface: Is this left out as a precaution in case some horrid rat sticks its nose in?
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges IN CASE and 'pokes ... in' puts R, the rodent's head, among those letters. The whole clue also describes the poison laid down for vermin.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic is a poison traditionally put down to kill rats and mice.

clue.text: Issue often associated with Lumière

definitions.meaning: the French sound-and-light spectacle pairs this word with lumière in its name

explanation.definitionFit: Issue in the sense of offspring includes a male child, and the French phrase pairs the word with lumière.

clue.text: Swimmer goes round team that's got less wind

indicators.note: turning around makes the swimmer's word face the other way, read backwards

parts.note: an eel is a swimming fish
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A swimmer passes around a team that has run out of puff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes round' reverses only the swimmer; 'less wind' is not about breath but the sheltered side.
explanation.definitionFit: The lee side of a ship or hill is the sheltered one, away from where the wind blows.

clue.text: Bank pursues wrong church in good faith

indicators.note: pursues means the bank's word chases along behind the other pieces

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
CE is the Church of England
to bank on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: A bank goes after a church for its misconduct.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something sincerely is to mean it honestly, which is acting in good faith.

clue.text: Perhaps skate across Tees in a huff

indicators.note: across means spanning the other piece, so the fish's word straddles the letters

parts.note: a skate is one kind of ray, a flat fish
two Ts spelt out as letter names

explanation.surface: A skater, perhaps, sulking as they cross the River Tees.
explanation.walkthrough: Tees is read as the letter T twice, not as the river in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is British informal for irritable or bad-tempered, the mood of someone sulking.
